rules.title: Wrap errors with context
rules.body: Return errors with what was being done, using %w so callers can inspect the cause: fmt.Errorf("load invoice %d: %w", id, err). Never discard an error with _ = err or an empty if err != nil {} block; compare sentinel errors with errors.Is and typed errors with errors.As, never by matching err.Error() text.

rules.title: Context comes first and flows down
rules.body: Functions that do I/O or may block take ctx context.Context as their first parameter and pass it to every call below them. Do not store a context in a struct, and do not call context.Background() or context.TODO() outside main, tests and top-level background loops.

rules.title: Every goroutine has an owner and an end
rules.body: A goroutine is started only where the code also knows how it stops: it ends on ctx.Done(), a closed channel or a WaitGroup that the starter waits on. Errors from goroutines are returned (errgroup) or logged, never lost.

rules.title: Close what you open, right after the error check
rules.body: Put defer rows.Close(), defer resp.Body.Close() and defer f.Close() on the line after the error check that follows opening them, and check rows.Err() after iterating. HTTP clients get explicit timeouts.

rules.title: Table-driven tests with t.Helper
rules.body: New tests use table-driven cases (a slice of structs with a name, run with t.Run) when they check the same function with different inputs. Test helpers call t.Helper(). Tests never sleep to wait for goroutines; they synchronise on channels or use polling with a deadline.

rules.title: Accept interfaces, return concrete types
rules.body: Declare small interfaces where they are used (in the consumer's package), and return concrete types from constructors. Do not add an interface with a single implementation unless a test or another package needs to replace it.
